name: Chrome Compliance: The Augmentation Mandate Files
description: A clandestinely produced documentary compiling internal corporate communications, medical records obtained through data breaches, and direct testimony from Shelf residents who underwent mandatory chrome augmentation under the 2208 Axiom Productivity Enhancement Directive, which publicly framed the program as voluntary. The film meticulously documents the coercive mechanisms — debt leverage, housing access restrictions, ration tier adjustments — used to ensure compliance among Tier 1 residents who had no practical ability to refuse. It was assembled by a collective of four documentarians operating under shared pseudonyms and released simultaneously across seventeen pirate mesh nodes.
cultural_impact: The documentary's internal memo — in which an Axiom productivity officer writes 'consent is a resource allocation question' — became one of the most widely reproduced pieces of text in Shelf graffiti culture, appearing on walls across the Stack for years after the film's release.
story_hooks: One of the detained collective members has recently been released and is behaving strangely — either broken, turned, or carrying information they cannot safely surface.
A player character recognizes a family member in the documentary's testimony footage, someone who told them the augmentation was their own choice.
The seventeenth mesh node that received the original simultaneous release was inside a Tier 4 residential complex — someone with serious access was involved, and they have never been identified.
